results.title: Stuffed crocs, holy water, llama foetus: Unusual things found at NZ borders in 2018
results.description: Fresh produce is expected to be one of the most common items confiscated at the border this summer, but some much more unusual things have been found with travellers this year (2018).
results.fulltext: Last summer, officials intercepted 3111 fresh produce items at New Zealand's borders - and they're expecting more this summer due to predicated increases in international visitors. Here's a round-up of some of the other items travellers turned up with at airports and on a cruise ship. 1. Stuffed crocodile ornaments A baggage search of a group of plane passengers returning from Vietnam revealed more than 40 stuffed crocodile ornaments. The ornaments were found to be contaminated with live beetle larvae and were treated. Officials handed them over to the Department of Conservation to check whether they complied with the rules around endangered species. However, the travellers did not have the required import permits and DOC ordered for the items to be destroyed. 2. Holy water Air passengers returning from India declared a bag of holy water to officers at Auckland Airport. The water had a green tinge, and on closer inspection, officers discovered a live shrimp. 3. Dried llama foetus Officials seized a dried llama foetus from a German backpacker, who declared it at Auckland Airport. The traveller told officials it was purchased in South America, thinking it was plastic. llama foetuses are associated with good luck in some parts of South America. 4. Tick attached to passenger A passenger arriving from the UK at Christchurch Airport declared a tick attached to her arm. Paramedics removed the tick, which was later identified as the castor bean tick. The species is associated with bacterial and viral pathogens, including Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis. 5. Cockatoo In February, Biosecurity NZ dealt with "the event of the summer" when they had to wrangle a cockatoo that decided to come across the Tasman on a cruise ship. The bird enjoyed a luxury cruise around New Zealand after biosecurity officials allowed it to stay on the vessel for eventual return, however subject to strict conditions. "We needed photographic evidence of its containment and the name of an officer responsible for looking after the bird. There was also a requirement for MPI officers to check on the bird and its containment facilities at every new port visit in New Zealand," Andrew Spelman, MPI's border clearance services manager said. Officials then took measures to rehabilitate it with its owner in Brisbane. 6. Bat's head In June, MPI faced a "nightmare" situation when a bat's head was declared at Auckland Airport by a passenger arriving from Apia. The traveller told officials his family had eaten the rest of the bat in Samoa and he wanted to show the head to relatives in New Zealand. The head was partly mummified with "loose flaps of skin", Biosecurity New Zealand passenger manager Craig Hughes said. "It was a biosecurity nightmare. Bats have a terrible reputation as disease carriers and the remains could have harboured hitchhiker pests." Biosecurity confiscated and destroyed the head. 7. Fruit fly larvae Another potential pest problem was posed in July when fruit fly larvae was intercepted at Auckland Airport. The larvae could have devastated the country's horticulture industry, Biosecurity New Zealand said. It was discovered in chillies the luggage of a tour party leader from Malaysia last month, after an x-ray screening. A caterpillar was also found in some garlic bulbs. The intercepted larvae were believed to be of Malaysian fruit fly, which has invaded a number of Pacific islands. The species attacks more than 60 types of fruit and vegetables.

attempts to accomplish this we find the reason for embalming among the ancient egyptians their pyramids their secret burials ana the extraordinary methods of hiding the dead customs which have been of natives of the northt-welit embalmed their dead the body was usually doubled up and placed in a case of fur or grass made for the purpose the alaskan commercial company secured from the seal islands of the company a mummy supposed to be 150 years old which shows that this method of burial has been followed for many years it was discovered on a cave in kagamale island filled with sulphurous vapours which came from crevices in the rock eleven mummies were found one the chief was held by a basket like coffin or structure 4ft in height and evidently made with the greatest care the material with which the remains were wrapped were matting woven from seaweed in a very skilful manner and1 skins amongl which was a fine skin of the sea otter over all was a net made of the sinews of the sea history of life upon the globe according to the first of these hypothesis life such a3 we now know it haa existed from all eternity upon this earth we tested that hypothesis by the circumstantial in his great poem i pointed out to you that the evidence at our command as completely and fully negatives that hypothesis as it did the preceding one and i confess that i had two much respect for your existing condition and the causes which have led to it of the animal and vegetable world an argument has been put forward as an objection to evolution which we shall have to consider very beriously i service that has been rendered by mr darwin to the doctrine of evolution in general is this that he has shown that there are two great factors in the process of evolution and one of them is the tendency to vary the existence of which may be proved by observation in all living forms the other is the influence of surrounding conditions on what i may call the parent form and the variations which are thus evolved from it if the surrounding conditions are such that the parent form is more competent to deal with them and flourish in them than the derived forms then in the struggle for existence the parent form will maintain itself and the derived forms will be exterminated but if on the contrary the conditions are buch as to be better for the derived than for the parent form the parent form will be extirpated and the derived form will take its place in the first case there will be no progression no advance of type through any imaginable series of ages in the second place of these persistent types of life is no obstacle in the way of the theory of evolution at all therefore this objection is no objection at all the facts of this character and they are numerous belong to that class of evidence which i have called in different that is to say they may be no direct support to the doctrine of evolution but they are perfectly capable of being interpreted in consistency with it a few years ago no remains of birds had been found below the tertiary rocks and i am not sure but that some persons were prepared to demonstrate that they could not have existed at an earlier modify the definition of the classes of birds and reptiles before tho production of a creature such as this it might have been said that a bird had such and such characteristics among which were an absence of teeth but the discovery of a bird that had teeth shows at once that there were ancient birds that in that particular respect approached reptiles more nearly than any existing bird does i results.fulltext: chapter iv a difficult koad jack benbow was awakened the next morning by the pouring rain it lasted mi day the baked earth steamed as hot bricks do when water is spilt on them and door of his tent and announced himself as better but when he consult ed jack about his daughter who he feared was sickening with the fever the young man was filled with remorse i think wed better stay here for the day said jack the rain does not look like stopping and the rest ruay do your daughter good yes i suppose we must as we get nearer our goal the difficulties seem to increase mrs lancaster is far from well this morning jack devoted his energies to the preparation of food he exercised all his ingenuity to cook something that agatha might be tempted to eat alas it was the only service he could render the next morning the sun shone out brightly and the waggons were soon on the move jack had to insist on the professor leaving his beetles to look after the drivers while he himself made a journey in search of poultry and eggs he succeeded in obtaining a supply from a mashuna kraal but had to tramp many a weary mile through the stifling heat the sun seemed to shine out all the hotter comforting news that she did not refuse the food he had been at such pains to prepare thus they journeyed for a week gradually descending to the lower country every day the travelling proved more difficult the oxen grew weaker the atmosphere more stifling and oppressive the native inhabitants became less numerous and their nights were constantly disturbed by the roaring of lions a little rain fell but not enough to fill the dried-up spruits or hinder their advance much of their way led over burnt-up plains and stony ridges where the new grass had not yet begun to sprout and the cattle got and more on jack gun he made a point of keeping out of agatha way but he watched over her welfare as never man watched before making use of pambana as go-between she kept much within her tent seemed the deep i spruit that barred their progress that i afternoon the rivers ate all running to our left now and are increasing in size lam sure we must be nearing it from what th mashunas eaid there arg wide plains to cross we are still among the hills yes but they are much lower now my barometer shows that we are only a thousand feet above the sea salisbury is nearly five thousand i shant feel safe from fever until we begin to rise again is mrs lancaster better not much she is having a severe attack lam afraid agatha will sicken next she has not been at all like herself for a week past i must shoot some more guineafowl there seem to be plenty about replied jack he would have liked to tell lancaster the true cause of his daughter indisposition but could hardly have done so without exposing his wife unfaithfulness i must try to find a kraal to-morrow but the niggers about here either have not much food or wont part with it cannot we get a supply of eggs i could eat them when everything else was distasteful we are getting into lower country each day and this is the spring fever season cant have much farther to go i am sure these are the imbezi mountains we must push on and drive the
